We need propose 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So overall: a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings, and on second phenyl a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (anilide with an aniline at other end). So three disconnections suggested: 1) amide formation (carboxylic acid to amide) between α,β-unsaturated acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). 2) Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. 3) sulfonamide formation between sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl source) and aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). So retrosynthesis steps: target -> break amide -> get α,β-unsaturated acid (C=CC(=O)O attached to phenyl) and aniline. Then break unsaturated acid via Doebner: get aromatic aldehyde (p-? the phenyl with sulfonamide) and malonic acid. Then break sulfonamide: get sulfonyl chloride (maybe p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the first phenyl). So final precursors: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl) and aniline (the second phenyl with NH2) and malonic acid. Actually need also the aromatic aldehyde: the phenyl bearing sulfonamide and methyl? The aldehyde is the same phenyl ring with sulfonamide attached? Wait the sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl ring (first phenyl). The unsaturated acid side chain is attached to second phenyl (the one attached to sulfonyl). Actually structure: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So sulfonamide connects first phenyl (tolyl) to second phenyl (para-substituted). The unsaturated amide side chain is on second phenyl. So Doebner modification would form the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to second phenyl (the aldehyde is that phenyl with sulfonamide). So aldehyde: c2ccc(SO2N... )c? Actually the aldehyde would be the phenyl with sulfonamide and a formyl group at para position relative to sulfonamide? In target, the side chain is at para position to sulfonamide on second phenyl. So aldehyde would be that phenyl with sulfonamide and CHO at that position. So we need that aldehyde as precursor.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Step1 (retro amide): break C(=O)N bond -> get α,β-unsaturated acid (C=CC(=O)O attached to phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Template: amide formation forward is coupling agent; retro is amide bond cleavage.

Step2 (retro Doebner): break C=C and C-CO2H bond to get aromatic aldehyde (phenyl with sulfonamide and CHO) and malonic acid.

Step3 (retro sulfonamide): break S-N bond to get sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). Actually the sulfonamide attaches the first phenyl (tolyl) to the second phenyl via sulfonyl group. So retro: sulfonamide cleavage gives sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and the second phenyl amine (the phenyl with sulfonamide). Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to first phenyl (tolyl) as N? Actually SMILES: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. The N is attached to the tolyl ring (aniline). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (aniline). The sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So retro sulfonamide: break N-S bond to give tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) attached to second phenyl (i.e., aryl sulfonyl chloride). The second phenyl is the sulfonyl aryl part (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride (p-? the second phenyl with substituent at para position (the side chain). So the sulfonyl chloride is something like ClSO2-Ph-? Actually aryl sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-Ph-? The phenyl has the side chain (the unsaturated acid) at para position relative to sulfonyl group. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is that phenyl with sulfonyl chloride at position where sulfonamide attaches. So we need that aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus final set of three reactions:

1) Amide formation: α,β-unsaturated acid + aniline -> target amide.

2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid.

3) Sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride -> aromatic aldehyde (aryl with sulfonamide) (the aldehyde precursor). Wait the aldehyde includes sulfonamide attached to tolyl? Actually after sulfonamide formation, we get the sulfonamide linking tolyl and aryl sulfonyl chloride, producing the sulfonamide product which is the aromatic aldehyde (since the aryl part still has aldehyde). So yes.

Now we need to find template IDs for each reaction. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria.

First, amide formation: functional_groups_broken: ["aliphatic carboxylic acid"]? Actually forward reaction: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide, breaking O-H and N-H, forming C-N. So broken functional group: aliphatic carboxylic acid (since acid is aliphatic? The acid is α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic, but still aliphatic carboxylic acid). Formed: amide. Use search.
